title: You built a platform… but your soul went silent.
paragraphs: You built a platform… but your soul went silent.

Because the louder the applause got…
the quieter your prayer life became.

Just posting.
Just sharing.
Just growing.

You stopped asking, “Lord, what do You want?”
And started asking, “Will this perform?”

You stopped seeking His presence…
and started chasing their reactions.

You have visibility—
but no vitality.

You have influence—
but no intimacy.
And it’s eating you alive in silence.

Somewhere along the way…
it stopped being about impact.

That moment the Holy Spirit nudged you…
and you scrolled past it.
Here’s the truth we don’t like to admit:

You can look anointed in public
and be empty in private.

You can speak about God
and slowly stop walking with Him.

You can gain followers
and lose your fear of the Lord.
“Be careful not to practice your righteousness in front of others to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.”

You may gain attention.
You may gain applause.
You may even gain influence.
Because God is not impressed by performance.
And then there’s this piercing truth:
“For they loved human praise more than the praise of God.”

Not just influence—
but addiction to approval.
Some scholars interpret this as a warning about religious leaders who feared losing status more than losing God’s presence.
You didn’t mean to replace God.
You just slowly started needing people more than Him.

Their comments became your comfort.
Their reactions became your reward.
Their attention became your identity.
You started performing instead of surrendering.
The Gospel doesn’t expose you to destroy you.
It exposes you to restore you.

Because this is where influence dies…
and impact is born.

Not just in actions…
but in motives.

We wanted to be seen.
We wanted to be praised.
We wanted to be enough—without God.
And sin separates us from Him.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”

Including the one holding the microphone.
Including the one with the platform.
Including you.
But God didn’t leave us there.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Not when you were pure.
Not when your motives were clean.
Not when your heart was right.
While you were still chasing influence—
To break the power of your need for human approval.
To bring you back to the Father.
You don’t have to earn your worth.
You don’t have to build your name.
You don’t have to perform for love.

“Jesus… I made it about me.
But I want to make it about You again.”
God is not asking you to delete your platform.
He’s asking you to purify your purpose.

Because influence surrendered to Jesus
becomes impact that echoes in eternity.
And only one voice will matter:
Save this so you never forget what really matters.
If this stirred something in you…
